topic: interpreting a fraction of a whole number or set (grades 4-5)
subtitle: Finding one equal group as a unit fraction of a set, finding several equal groups as a non unit fraction, and working backwards from a part to the whole

problems.note: 24 crayons split into 4 equal groups; one group is one fourth.
21 stickers into 3 equal rows; one row is one third.
18 marbles into 3 equal groups of 6, then take 2 of those groups.

traps.desc: divided by the top number and multiplied by the bottom one

problems.note: 32 pages into 4 equal groups of 8, then take 3 of them.

traps.desc: stopped after making the groups and reported just one group

problems.note: Backwards: one fifth of the bag is 8 grapes, so the bag holds 5 groups of 8.
42 minutes into 6 equal parts of 7, then take 5 of them.
One eighth of a 2.4 litre jug; the same 'one equal group' idea on a measured amount.

traps.desc: multiplied by 8 instead of splitting the 2.4 litres into 8 equal parts

problems.note: Two steps: three sevenths of 28 ride the bus, and the question asks for the rest.

traps.desc: answered how many DO ride the bus instead of how many do not

problems.note: Backwards with a non-unit fraction: 3 groups are 96 seats, so one group is 32 and the whole is 8 groups.
Error analysis: the planted answer takes one of the five equal groups instead of three.

traps.desc: made the five equal groups but then took only one of them
